scholarships.title: Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarship for 2027 - Research Students (Embassy Recommendation)
scholarships.official_source: Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology (MEXT), Japan - administered in-country through Japanese embassies/consulates

existing.description: The MEXT Scholarship research-student route funds postgraduate research study at a Japanese graduate school: it exempts tuition, pays a monthly scholarship of ¥143,000-¥145,000, and provides round-trip travel expenses (airfare). Recipients are selected by the Japanese embassy or consulate general in their country after sitting that mission's Japanese and English qualifying examinations, and are then placed at a graduate school. This record covers the Embassy Recommendation route for the 2027 cohort; the separate University Recommendation route is administered by individual Japanese universities.
eligibility: Research students: You must be under 35 years of age and be eligible for admission to a master's program or a doctoral program (first or second stage) at a Japanese graduate school.
Embassy Recommendation: scholarship recipients are recruited and initially screened by a Japanese embassy (or consulate general, depending on the country).

The type and field of application may vary from country to country. Please check with the Japanese embassy or other Japanese diplomatic mission in your country to see if there are any openings in the type and field you wish to apply for.
All required documents and interviews will be conducted by the Japanese embassy or other diplomatic mission abroad in your country.
existing.eligibility_summary: Research students must be under 35 years of age and be eligible for admission to a master's programme or a doctoral programme (first or second stage) at a Japanese graduate school.
benefits: Preliminary training of Japanese etc. of 6 months for those who need this training, where offered by the institution
Placement into a Japanese graduate school at no application cost
coverage: Monthly scholarship of ¥143,000-¥145,000 per month for research students
Preliminary training of Japanese etc.: 6 months (only those who need this training)
requirements: Application must be made through a Japanese embassy or consulate general in the applicant's own country (Embassy Recommendation route).
Applicants must take the embassy/consulate's qualifying examinations, which for research students are Japanese and English.
The applicant must submit a 'Configuration Preference for University of Placement' (配置希望大学申請書) as part of the application forms.
Application fee is not charged; MEXT warns that organisations or individuals charging application fees or deposits have no relation with the Japanese Government.

Field of Specialization and Research Plan (専攻分野及び研究計画) - PDF

application_method: Confirm with the Japanese embassy or consulate general in your own country whether the Research Student type and the field you wish to apply for are open this year.
Sit the embassy/consulate's qualifying examinations for research students (Japanese and English).

Complete the MEXT application forms: Application Form, Configuration Preference for University of Placement, Field of Specialization and Research Plan, Certificate of Health, and the University Acceptance Consent format.
Submit all required documents and attend the interview conducted by the Japanese embassy or consulate general in your country.
The embassy/consulate screens applicants and forwards its recommendations to MEXT.
MEXT makes the scholarship offer and the receiving graduate school is identified for placement.
Receive round-trip airfare funded by MEXT and begin study in Japan.
existing.selection_notes: Applicants are recruited and initially screened by the Japanese embassy or consulate general in their country, which sits its own qualifying examinations (Japanese and English for research students), conducts the interview and collects all required documents; MEXT then selects the scholarship students and allocates them to host graduate schools, subject to the host university's acceptance.
existing.best_fit: Applicants who already hold (or are close to) a bachelor's degree and can enter a Japanese graduate school's master's or doctoral programme, who are under 35, who sit the embassy/consulate's Japanese and English examinations, and whose country runs the Research Student track.
existing.notes: No published deferral, renewal, return-home or clinical-restriction terms were readable on the official pages read. MEXT publishes rules on extending the scholarship period (applications for extension from newly admitted students in April 2026 and from early-completers are handled by notice), rules on combining the scholarship with other awards, and rules on part-time work by scholarship students, but these notices are in Japanese and were not readable in the English sources used for this record. Application is free of charge.
existing.duration: Embassy Recommendation: irregular course within 2 years; regular course: standard school year (when necessary, 6 months preliminary education will be added)
existing.application_period: Applications for the 2027 cycle are handled at embassy/consulate level. MEXT lists the 2027 Embassy Recommendation Research Student recruitment under "募集中のプログラム" (programmes currently being recruited). No central opening or closing date is published; embassies set and publish their own deadlines and sit their own qualifying examinations.
existing.deadline_display: No central deadline is published. MEXT states that all procedures for the Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarships are conducted through Japanese embassies, consulates in your countries, or institutions of higher education in Japan; candidates should contact the Japanese embassy (or consulate general) in their own country for the application date, and the Study in Japan page states that the type and field of application may vary from country to country and that applicants should check with the Japanese embassy or other Japanese diplomatic mission for any openings.
